47c8 AC: 'A ticket created in-process is returned by the next query in that same process...' — actor is 'query', one level below 'create'
80a5 ACs exercise retrieval via injection: 'A create exits 0 with an empty similar_tickets when retrieval returns empty... when retrieval raises' — neither drives a real index

findings.finding: Parent AC6 ('A ticket created on a clone is findable by the next create on that same clone, in one process, with no daemon... Checked by: an integration test') is only partially covered. Child 47c8's nearest criterion asserts a ticket is 'returned by the next QUERY in that same process' at the query-API level, not by the next CREATE; child 80a5's surfacing tests inject empty/raising retrieval rather than exercising a live index. No child's integration test asserts an actual create surfacing a prior actual create end to end.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child 80a5 (or 47c8) with an integration-test criterion exercising a real create→create against the live lexical index, asserting the prior ticket surfaces, matching parent AC6's actor and scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State what the advisory 'score' represents and whether/how it is normalized to be comparable across the lexical (bm25) and embedding (cosine) tiers.
evidence: 'returns at most 5 similar existing tickets as an advisory field carrying id, alias, title and score'
Lexical tier uses 'bm25 weights title 5.0 / description 1.0'; embedding tier uses 'vector ranking' — different score scales
E2 signal (2): a derived metric with no computation/aggregation protocol is a data-design ambiguity
findings.finding: The advisory's 'score' field has no stated computation or cross-tier normalization protocol. The lexical tier ranks by bm25 and the embedding tier by vector similarity (cosine), which are on different scales, yet the advisory carries a single 'score' field consumed identically across all four surfaces.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, line 1 ('an advisory field carrying id, alias, title and score')
scenarios: A consumer or test asserts on 'score' values but the number means bm25 in lexical mode and cosine similarity in embedding mode, breaking any threshold logic
The shape test can't assert a meaningful range for 'score'
findings.suggested_fix: Specify a stated range (e.g. normalized 0..1) or declare score as tier-opaque rank-ordering only, and say which the shape tests assert.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a covering acceptance criterion for the Bedrock IAM widening (e.g. an attestation that the Titan embedding model is reachable in this deployment), or mark the child as deliberately AC-free with rationale.
evidence: Child bullet: 'Bedrock IAM widening for the Titan embedding model — admits the configured default embedding model in this deployment'
No AC references IAM, Bedrock permissions, or the Titan model being reachable in this deployment
E1: every described deliverable should have a covering criterion
findings.finding: The 'Bedrock IAM widening for the Titan embedding model' child has no covering acceptance criterion. Every other child maps to at least one AC, but this deliverable (an IAM policy change) is described only in the decomposition with no criterion verifying it was performed.
scenarios: The IAM change is skipped and the default embedding tier silently fails in this deployment, with nothing marking the child incomplete

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that verifies the embedding tier is exercised when a provider is configured (and, if feasible in-session, that its ranking is applied rather than silently degrading to lexical).
evidence: Child: 'the digest step, the configured embedding model, vector ranking, and the empties and retry counters ADR 0122 requires'

ACs cover 'at most 5', the four surfaces, lexical-tier no-provider retrieval, and failure modes — none assert embedding-tier ranking behaviour or that vector ranking is used when a provider is configured
findings.finding: The embedding-tier child promises vector ranking that must beat the measured baseline (ADR 0122 recall@5 0.876 vs lexical 0.823), but no acceptance criterion verifies the embedding tier's retrieval quality or that it is actually exercised when a provider is configured — the ACs are tier-agnostic or lexical-specific.
findings.location: Child decomposition, 'Embedding tier over the pydantic-ai embeddings seam'; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: Embedding tier is wired but defective (e.g. always falls back to lexical) and no criterion catches it

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, per retrieval failure arm, the disposition it surfaces using an explicit disposition word (embedding-provider throttle = retryable/transient vs auth denial / digest-parse-empty = fatal), and state which disposition wins when the embedding tier falls back — confirming the lexical fallback never masks a retryable embedding failure from the diagnostic.
evidence: 'A create succeeds with an empty or lexical-only advisory when the index is absent, when catch-up fails, when the configured embedding provider denies or errors, and when the digest parse yields empty fields.'
'the empties and retry counters ADR 0122 requires of any consumer' (embedding-tier child implies retry semantics whose disposition is unstated)

ABSENCE: no explicit disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) is attached to the embedding-provider-error arm, and no statement that a transient embedding throttle is distinguished from the lexical fallback's success
findings.finding: The plan adds a two-tier fallback chain (embedding tier -> lexical tier -> empty advisory) and enumerates its failure arms ('index absent, catch-up fails, embedding provider denies or errors, digest parse yields empty fields'), but it states only a uniform create-side disposition ('create succeeds with an empty or lexical-only advisory') and never assigns an explicit disposition word per arm. In particular, a retryable embedding-provider throttle (e.g. a Bedrock 429 / WAIT_AND_RETRY) is folded into the same silent lexical-only degradation as a permanent auth denial, so the recoverable leg is not preserved or surfaced — the 1c0d masking shape at the retrieval layer.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'A create succeeds with an empty or lexical-only advisory when the index is absent, when catch-up fails, when the configured embedding provider denies or errors...'
scenarios: A configured Bedrock embedding model returns a 429 throttle on a create; the plan degrades silently to a lexical-only advisory + diagnostic, so the transient/retryable nature of the embedding failure is indistinguishable from a permanent credential denial to any consumer reading the result or diagnostic.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Failure-disposition contract' note to the epic (or push it into the embedding-tier child's ACs): classify the embedding arm's errors (transient throttle vs permanent auth/parse) so the emitted diagnostic carries the retryable vs fatal distinction even when the create itself degrades to lexical-only.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the IAM-widening child that the added resource ARN pins the specific Titan model (e.g. 'foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0'), not a broad 'amazon.*' wildcard, matching the existing narrow Claude-only scoping in iam_s7.tf.
evidence: Child text: 'admits the configured default embedding model in this deployment' — states the model but not the ARN scoping.
Existing policy is tightly scoped: resources are 'arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-*' and an account-constrained 'inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*' (iam_s7.tf:15-18).
ADR/epic comment names the exact model id 'amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0', so a pinned ARN is achievable without a wildcard.
findings.finding: The 'Bedrock IAM widening' child names the model to admit but does not specify least-privilege ARN scoping for the new grant, leaving open whether it pins the specific Titan model-id ARN (matching the existing narrow Claude pattern) or widens to a broader amazon.* wildcard.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Bedrock IAM widening for the Titan embedding model'; infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:15-18
scenarios: The child's implementer adds 'foundation-model/amazon.*' or a broad embedding wildcard rather than the specific titan-embed-text-v2:0 ARN, broadening the grant beyond what the feature needs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the child: 'Add a resource ARN pinned to arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 (plus the matching inference-profile ARN if cross-region inference is used), preserving the Claude-only statement's least-privilege scoping — no amazon.* wildcard.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the embedding-tier child, co-locate the digest failure-handling rule with the digest schema: define what distinguishes a retriable non-answer from a parse-empty, the retry count/bound, which counter (`empties` vs retry) increments in each case and where, and that a terminal empty degrades to lexical-only.
evidence: Plan: the embedding child carries '... the empties and retry counters ADR 0122 requires of any consumer.'

ADR 0122 Consequences: 'The digest parser silently returned empty fields for three distinct reply shapes ... each indistinguishable from success without a failure counter' and 'Two tickets in 630 did not answer the digest task at all ... a retry is the correct handling.'

Both a non-answering task and a parse-empty surface as empty digest fields, yet neither plan nor ADR states when to retry vs. when to count toward `empties` and degrade, nor the retry count/bound, nor where the counter increments relative to the lexical fallback.
The failure-mode AC lists 'digest parse yields empty fields' but does not name the nondeterministic non-answer-then-retry case as a distinct, bounded behavior.
findings.finding: The digest sub-step references two counters (`empties` and `retry`) and two overlapping failure handlings — count-empty-and-fall-back vs. retry — but the decision rule separating them, the retry bound, and the counter-increment placement are not specified in the plan or ADR.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Embedding tier over the pydantic-ai embeddings seam'; AC 'A create succeeds with an empty or lexical-only advisory when ... the digest parse yields empty fields'
scenarios: Haiku returns a prose preamble around valid JSON (parse-empty) — executor must decide retry or degrade
A ticket's digest reply does not perform the digest task at all — ADR says retry, but the bound and the distinguishing signal are unspecified

findings.finding: Owned-by-none scope gap: the initial full-corpus embedding backfill and its interaction with the shared Bedrock daily spend cap is named by the epic as a prerequisite to be settled in the index-and-surfacing child's plan, but no child under this container owns it. Child 2041 owns the per-ticket digest-and-embed build step and is the only Bedrock-calling path, yet neither it, 47c8, nor f10f addresses how the first corpus backfill is run or bounded against the account-wide cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a criterion to child 2041 specifying how the initial corpus backfill is run and bounded (e.g. throttle under the metered ceiling or run the one-time backfill deliberately), or create a sibling that owns it, so the epic-deferred prerequisite has an owner.
